title: Extreme Heat Warning
description: The National Weather Service has issued an Extreme Heat Warning through Friday August 28th for the Las Vegas and Lake Mead area. Visitors should limit outdoor activities on land within the recreation area, drink plenty of water, and be alert for symptoms of heat illness including thirst, heavy sweating, muscle cramps, weakness/dizziness, headache, and nausea. Anyone experiencing these symptoms should move indoors in air conditioning immediately.

title: Hans Flat Ranger Station Temporarily Closed
description: Hans Flat Ranger Station is temporarily closed so onsite personnel can focus on an ongoing search operation. For updated road conditions, trip planning, or other questions about The Maze, email Canyonlands' Backcountry Office at canyres@nps.gov.

title: West Nile Virus detected in Mosquito Samples at the Floyd Estate, FI Pines
description: West Nile Virus has been detected at the William Floyd Estate and Fire Island Pines from mosquito samples collected on August 12, 2026. Increased surveillance of mosquitoes in the area will continue. It is recommended visitors limit or forego outdoor activities between dusk and dawn.

title: Hiker's Lot Closed
description: Due to an issue with a telecommunication line, the Hiker's Parking Lot is temporarily closed. Visitors can continue to park at the Main Parking Lot as a starting point for their visit to Carl Sandburg Home.

title: Towpath Trail Improvements
description: Hunt House Trailhead to north end of Beaver Marsh boardwalk closed from Monday, August 17 at 7 am to Friday, September 18 at 5 pm. Weekdays only, open on weekends. Beaver marsh open and accessible via Ira Trailhead. Boston Trailhead to Lock 29 in Peninsula: August 24–November 20, 2026 and March 29–April 21, 2027.

title: Special Event: September 19 & 26, 2026 - Temporary Closures of Scenic Drive
description: Reef Ride Bike Days: For this special event in honor of National Public Lands Day, the Scenic Drive will be closed to motor vehicles for part of the day on Saturday, September 19 and Saturday, September 26, 2026. The road will be closed to vehicles from sunrise to 3 pm to allow for bicycles and pedestrians to enjoy the road at a more leisurely pace. The main road through the park (UT highway 24) - will remain open and unaffected by this closure.

title: WILDFIRE CLOSURES: Sunrise, White River, & northern trails.
description: Due to several active fires on the north side of the park, the following closures are in effect until further notice: Sunrise & White River Roads, Grand Park area & trails, Northern Loop Trail, Wonderland Trail from Carbon River Suspension Bridge to White River Campground, & associated backcountry campgrounds.

title: Stay Away From Bull Elk
description: Bull elk are fast and unpredictable this time of year and can seriously injure people. If an elk charges, run. In addition to staying at least 25 yards (23 m) away from elk and bison, always stay at least 100 yards (91 m) away from bears and wolves.

title: Cedar Breaks Water Service Interruption
description: Due to a water service interruption, drinking water is currently unavailable throughout Cedar Breaks National Monument. Flush toilets and campground showers are also unavailable; visitors may use the pit/vault toilets in the picnic area.

title: For Visitor information or assistance, Call (334) 727-3200
description: For visitor information or assistance at Tuskegee Institute National Historic Site, please call (334) 727-3200.For group reservations please call Sheryl Buchanan at (334) 421-3246.

title: The Oaks Tours by Reservation Only
description: The Oaks, the historic home of Booker T. Washington, is open by reservation only during an ongoing construction and preservation project. Built in 1899, the Queen Anne-style home is undergoing exterior rehabilitation work. Tours are limited to a maximum of 5 visitors per reservation. Large groups and walk-in tours will not be accommodated during this time. To make a reservation, please call (334) 727-3200 or (334) 421-3246.

title: Sulphur Banks Bridge Closed; Boardwalk is Open
description: The Sulphur Banks Bridge is damaged and closed until further notice. The Haʻakulamanu area, boardwalk and Sulphur Banks Trail are open and accessible from the west side near Steam Vents.

title: Kahuku Unit Closed Until Further Notice
description: The Kahuku Unit is closed following Hurricane Lala which impacted the Kaʻū District the hardest. Staff are assessing damage to roads, trails and other infrastructure.

title: Lees Ferry Campground Partial Closure
description: The upper loop of the Lees Ferry Campground is closed for renovations. Large equipment will be paving at the Lees Ferry campground. Do not enter construction area.

title: Crews Responding to Mount Tom Creek and Mt. Barnes Fires
description: Fire managers are responding to two lightning fires in a remote areas Olympic National Park. The Mount Tom Creek Fire has burned 69 acres 5 miles west-northwest of Mount Olympus. The Mt. Barnes Fire has burned 0.5 acres 1.5 miles southeast of Mt. Barnes. Firefighters are using indirect confinement tactics as part of a full-suppression strategy. Backpackers are encouraged to consider alternative routes to the Hoh River Trail should fire activity increase. There are no evacuation orders or closures.

title: Water Outage
description: Visitor Center Water Outage! Due to a break in the water line, water is currently unavailable at the Visitor Center, including bathrooms and drinking fountains. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience while repairs are underway. We’ll provide an update when water service has been restored. Please plan accordingly if you are visiting the area. We recommend bringing 32oz of water per person for a cave visit.

title: Many Areas in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park Now Open
description: The remaining storm and safety closures that remain include Mauna Loa Road beyond the gate at Kīpukapuaulu, Kīpukapuaulu Trail, Nāmakanipaio Campground and cabins, the backcountry and the Kahuku Unit.

title: Good Luck Road Parking Lot Closed
description: The Good Luck Road Parking Lot is closed. Please use the main entrance located at 6565 Greenbelt Road, Greenbelt, MD 20770.

title: Trail Maintenance Underway Near Sand Cave
description: Crews are using Ridge Trail from Hensley to Sand Cave Trail to complete trail work. Trails remain open; some sections may be muddy or messy.

title: Guardrail Repair: Expect Construction Delays
description: Guardrail repair will take place from 8/25-8/28 and from 8/31-9/4. There will be no full road closures, but delays of up to 30 minutes are possible. Delays will be minimized from 6-9am and from 3:30-6pm. Work on the east side is between Devils Kitchen and Red Canyon Overlook. West side work is between the west entrance and Redlands View overlook. Please be alert for construction workers and flaggers.

title: Lower Cliff Dwelling Trail Closed due to Extreme Heat Warning.
description: The Lower Cliff Dwelling trail will be closed Tuesday, August 25th to Friday, August 28th. The trail will reopen Saturday, August 29th at 8:00 a.m.

title: Both Districts of Haleakalā are Now Open
description: Update 8/25/26: The Summit District of Haleakalā National Park is OPEN to the public after recovery from Tropical Storm Lala. This includes Haleakalā Crater and Hosmer Grove. Kīpahulu District, including Pīpīwai Trail, opened 8/20/26.

title: Trail Closures due to recent weather event
description: Wall Street, the Bryce Connector Trail (to Peekaboo Loop), Peekaboo Loop, and the Tropic Trail are closed until further notice.

title: Great Hall, Faneuil Hall Closures: September 2026
description: Due to scheduled events, the Great Hall will close early on September 2 and 11. The Visitor Center Desk on the market floor will remain open.

title: NPS 300 Road Conditions
description: NPS 300 to Big Tubes has not been evaluated since the most recent rainfall. A high clearance vehicle is recommended. The road past Big Tubes is very rough and only accessible to high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicles.

title: Bison are in the Breeding Season
description: A reminder that bison are going about their normal life cycle and may be more aggressive. A raised tail is a warning sign and the animal may charge or give chase. Please give a wide distance, at least 100 yards. There are other trails you may choose to hike without encountering the bison.

title: Auto-Theft Warning - Only Bring What You Need to the Park
description: You can prevent vehicle break-ins in parking lots and scenic overlooks. Before leaving your car for even a short period of time: 1) Remove all valuables, 2) Lock your doors. 3) Take your wallets, purses, backpacks, keys, key fobs, cell phones, and electronics with you. Read article for more details.

title: Trailhead Access at Horseshoe Canyon
description: Due to active search and rescue operations, visitors should refrain from accessing the main Horseshoe Canyon trailhead. Hans Flat Ranger Station and The Maze district are still accessible using dirt roads from UT 24 or Green River, Utah.

title: Abrams Falls Trail Closed
description: Abrams Falls Trail is closed Mondays-Thursdays through September 30 to replace aging footlog bridges and improve visitor safety. The trail will open to hikers Fridays-Sundays and on Labor Day during construction.

title: Increased Logging Traffic Along Swift Brook Road
description: Be alert for logging trucks along Swift Brook Road between the monument boundary and the start of the Loop Road. Logging trucks will be transporting logs on Swift Brook Road to Roberts Road. Logging trucks ALWAYS have the right of way. Keep your headlights on. Never stop on roads or bridges. Pull over to the side of the road to allow trucks to pass by.

title: Pinnacle Peak Trail - Plummer Peak Backcountry Area CLOSURE
description: 8/23/2026 - Due to active wildfire, Pinnacle Peak Trail and the surround area are CLOSED until further notice. This includes the ridge from Lane Peak to Foss Peak across the ridge and from Stevens Canyon Road to the southern park boundary. Stevens Canyon Road is NOT closed.

title: Park Status and Updates
description: For information on weather related updates and other park conditions like beach and hiking safety visit our park status page.

title: Pennsylvania Memorial Observation Deck Closed
description: A renovation project for the nearby Comfort Station requires electrical service to be shut off. This shut off affects lighting in the spiral staircase leading up to the Pennsylvania Memorial observation deck. The staircase is now too dark to maintain visitors’ safety. The observation deck will remain closed until the Comfort Station project is complete in early-to-mid November. Note: The base of the Pennsylvania Memorial remains open to visitation during this time.

title: Water Safety Alert
description: After recent storms, E. coli levels are likely to reach above safe swimming standards. Entering the water after heavy rainfall is never recommended. Know before you go and always check our Beach Safety page before heading to park beaches.

title: Beat the Heat
description: Make sure to take hot weather into consideration. Carry water and use sunscreen to reduce the risk of heat injuries during your visit.

title: Canaveral National Seashore: Delayed Opening Sunday August 30th
description: The Playalinda District of Canaveral National Seashore will have a delayed opening on Sunday, August 30, due to the Falcon Heavy rocket launch scheduled for 7:26 AM. NASA roadblocks will be established on the Max Brewer Bridge and the Haulover Canal bridge, Kennedy Parkway. Roadblocks will be lifted after successful launch or scrub. The Apollo district will open at its regular time of 6:00 AM.

title: Campfire ban lifted parkwide
description: Effective August 24, 2026, at 3:00 p.m., the National Park Service has lifted campfire restrictions in Voyageurs National Park due to cooler weather and a lower risk of wildfire. The lifting of these fire restrictions aligns with changes made by the U.S. Forest Service in the Superior National Forest and the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources.

title: Temporary Road Closures in Effect
description: The following roads are temporary closed: West Border Road (Roosevelt Reservation) from the Lukeville Port of Entry west to Quitobaquito Springs, East Border Road (Roosevelt Reservation) from the Lukeville Port of Entry east to the Santa Rosa Mountains, and Camino de Dos Republicas. See Alerts for more info.

title: Road Closure: Sunset Crater Volcano September 21 through October 21
description: Beginning September 21, Forest Road 545 will close to all vehicle traffic starting near the intersection with Highway 89A to the Sunset Crater Volcano entrance kiosk for culvert work. Sunset Crater Volcano National Monument remains OPEN and accessible via Forest Road 545 through Wupatki National Monument. Plan for extra travel time—the drive between visitor centers is about 19 miles/30 minutes. The road is expected to reopen October 22.

title: Road Closure: Sunset Crater Volcano September 21 through October 21
description: Beginning September 21, Forest Road 545 will close to all vehicle traffic starting near the intersection with Highway 89A to the Sunset Crater Volcano entrance kiosk for culvert work. Sunset Crater Volcano National Monument remains OPEN and accessible via Forest Road 545 through Wupatki National Monument. Plan for extra travel time—the drive between visitor centers is about 19 miles/30 minutes. The road is expected to reopen October 22.

title: South Shore Quinault Road Washed Out Beyond Park Boundary
description: South Shore Road – which is maintained by Jefferson County – is closed due to a major wash-out. For more information, visit the Jefferson County website.

title: Metcalf Bottoms Bridge is closed to pedestrians due to bridge damage
description: Metcalf Bottoms Bridge is closed to pedestrians due to bridge damage. Visitors will not be able to walk from the picnic area across the bridge to access the Metcalf Bottoms Trail. Parking for the trail is limited near the trailhead.

title: No Water Available at the Clarno Unit
description: There is currently no water available at the Clarno Unit of the park. Please plan accordingly and bring water when visiting.

title: North Beach and North Beach Road temporarily closed to visitors.
description: Point Reyes National Seashore has temporarily closed North Beach after a fishing vessel ran aground early on Friday, August 21st. No injuries or fuel leaks have been reported, and the National Park Service is coordinating with the U.S. Coast Guard, NOAA and Marin County Fire as the Coast Guard works to secure a contractor to remove fuel from the vessel. Visitors are asked to stay clear of North Beach while the closure remains in effect to allow first responders to work safely and without interference.

title: Great Sand Dunes Currently at Stage 1 Fire Restrictions
description: As of August 18th, Great Sand Dunes is under Stage 1 Fire Restrictions. All wood and charcoal fires must be in established fire rings in designated campsites or picnic sites. No other open fires are allowed. Fires MUST BE put out COLD before leaving your site and must not be left unattended. camp stoves and other pressurized gas devices allowed.

title: Manzanar Remains Open During US 395 Pavement Project
description: CalTrans begins a monthslong pavement project on US 395 adjacent to Manzanar National Historic Site on Monday, May 11, 2026. Crews will be working to ensure access to Manzanar remains open, but it will be important to travel cautiously as typical access may involve detours and map apps may be inaccurate. Though work is scheduled only during weekdays, lane closures and detours will be in place throughout the week. Currently, the site may only be accessed via the south entrance.

title: Toxic Algae Found – Blue Mesa Water Quality Advisory
description: Cyanotoxins are currently present in the Iola Basin. Until further notice, the park recommends that no person or pet swims in, or drinks from, reservoir waters in the Iola Basin. Use caution when fishing, boating, or recreating in Blue Mesa Reservoir.

title: America the Beautiful Passes Temporary Unavailable
description: At this time all sales of America the Beautiful Passes are temporary unavailable. Please check https://store.usgs.gov/recreational-passes for locations. We will advise when passes are available for sale. We apologize for any inconvenience.

title: Temporary Delays & Closures for Tennessee Valley Trails August 24 - Sept 4
description: Road crew will be traveling to work sites via Bobcat Trail to perform repair work on a section of Coastal Trail from the intersection of Fox to the intersection of Pirates Cove Trail. Work will start on August 24 and last for approximately two weeks. 8 AM to 4 PM Monday through Friday. Once that section is complete work will start from Pirates Cove to the intersection of Tennessee Valley. Please obey closures and stay away from work sites. Signage will be posted near trail and road intersections.

title: Food-Conditioned Bear in Arrigetch Peaks
description: On August 13, 2026 a brown bear entered camps and food caches in the Arrigetch Peaks area, obtaining food from a soft-sided, bag-type Bear Resistant Food Container (BRFC). At this time, we strongly recommend hard-sided BRFCs for all visitors to the Arrigetch Peaks area. Hard-sided BRFCs can be checked out at the Bettles Ranger Station. Backpackers in the area should maintain a high level of bear awareness and continue to follow best practices for camping in bear country.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Until further notice, the following are prohibited in all park areas: (1) Building, maintaining, attending, or using wood or charcoal fires anywhere but within campground- or picnic area-provided grills or grates. (The use of gas grills and camp stoves is permitted.) (2) Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle or while stopped in an area at least three feet in diameter that is barren of all flammable materials. (3) Discharging or using any kind of fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices.

title: Harmful Algal Blooms Occurring in Lake Richie and Intermediate Lake
description: Blooms are tested for toxin levels and monitored. Toxin levels are consistently low on Isle Royale. It is not recommended to filter water in any areas where there is surface scum, strong odors, or other evidence of a significant bloom. Blooms move around depending on wind and rain – filter water from places where blooms are not present or a different water source. It is low risk to filter water from relatively clear areas of an impacted water source.

title: Marblemount Bridge August-September Nighttime Closure
description: Skagit River Marblemount Bridge will be closed overnight for repairs August 24-September 4, Monday night-Friday morning, 8 pm-4 am. There is no access to Cascade River Road during the nighttime closure.

title: Island Mine Campground Stream Low
description: The stream has very little water flow. Campers should bring enough water to Island Mine or plan on collecting water at Carnelian Beach to the south.

title: Construction in the South End of the Park
description: Construction projects underway. Moose-Wilson Road between Murie Ranch and LS Rockefeller Preserve open with delays of 45 minutes in both directions. No roadside parking on Moose-Wilson Road. Expected to close 9/7. Taggart Trail detour in place. Menor's Ferry Road closed weekdays. Mormon Row area open with some construction activity.

title: Gauley Tailwaters Campground Closure
description: The Tailwaters Campground in Gauley River National Recreation Area, located below Summersville Dam, will temporarily close from September 11 through September 28 in order to allow for more parking and better river access during the busy Gauley season.

title: Mason's Branch Road Closure
description: Mason's Branch Road will be closed for necessary safety repairs from 07/29/26 through around 09/03/26. Check back for updates.

title: Open Season
description: Jumonville Glen, Mount Washington Tavern, and the Picnic Area are OPEN until October 31st. Jumonville Glen and the Picnic Area are open daily sunrise to sunset, and Mount Washington Tavern is open every day 10 am to 4 pm.

title: Farmington Landing CLOSED
description: The National Park Service is imposing a temporary closure of Farmington Landing. This temporary closure is necessary to provide for visitor safety during a comprehensive rehabilitation project to restore park resources and improve the visitor experience. Work will include resurfacing the parking lot, replacing parking barriers, replacing trash cans with new wildlife-proof trash cans, and installing new fishing rod holders. The National Park Service appreciates the public’s cooperation in this matter.

title: Amphitheater Trail temporarily closed for construction
description: The Amphitheater Trail is closed for ongoing construction. Visitors will not be able to use the trail between the campground and the visitor center.

description: Campsites, houseboat sites, and the day use sites are closed on Dryweed Island and nearby sites due to unsafe bear‑human interactions. Affected locations include Breakwater Cove, Dryweed Island, Harrison Bay, Makinen Point, Mio Beach, Stones Point, Loon Cove, Rock Shelf, Lyle Mine Island, Tango Channel, and Harrison Bay E. Overnight use and houseboat mooring are not allowed. For a full list of sites covered by the closure, click the link below:

title: Seasonal Closure: Bush Key
description: Visitors may only access the harborside of Bush Key through Fall 2026 to protect nesting Sooty Terns, Brown Noddies, and Magnificent Frigatebirds. Boaters must maintain a distance of 100 feet from the island's mean low tide.

title: Cunard, Nuttallburg Road Closures, Brooklyn CG Closure
description: The Cunard road is currently closed due to multiple slides, Brooklyn Campground is closed due to closure of the Cunard Road, Nuttallburg road is closed due to a washout. All closures are weather related.

title: Natural Entrance Trail Closed
description: Due to construction in the park, the Natural Entrance trail will be closed on Wednesday, August 26 and Thursday, August 27. Elevators will be the only way to enter and exit the cavern. Sorry for any inconvenience this may cause and thank you for understanding.

title: Carter G. Woodson Home NHS temporarily closed — will Reopen November 2026
description: The Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site is temporarily closed due to a full renovation project. The Grand Reopening of the site will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Please continue to visit the website for future updates.

title: Burn Ban in Park
description: Due to high fire danger, Hot Springs National Park has enacted a BURN BAN, August 15, 2026. Only gas and charcoal grills are currently allowed for use in the campground and picnic areas.

title: Temporary Partial Closure Redwood Creek Trail August 19 - Sept 4
description: A section of the boardwalk along the Redwood Creek Trail will be closed from Wednesday, August 19 through Friday, September 4. The closure area spans from just past Cathedral Grove to the junction with the Fern Creek Trail. A detour will be in place.

title: Campfires, charcoal fires, or other open fires are not allowed
description: Bryce Canyon is in Stage 2 Fire Restrictions. No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using of open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires, charcoal fires, and propane fire pits in park campgrounds. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is not permitted, except inside an enclosed vehicle. Fireworks are never permitted at Bryce Canyon National Park.

title: Temporary Closure - Douglas Center
description: The Paul H Douglas Center is closed until Wednesday 8/19, and all public programs are cancelled until further notice. Several parts of the park are inaccessible due to the weather event from August 11th. It is not advisable to go in the lake after a heavy rain. Use extreme caution when visiting as most locations have no power and are out of service.

title: Emergency Closure of Portions of Christiansted National Historic Site
description: Portions of Fort Christiansvaern and portions of D. Hamilton Jackson Park are temporarily closed due to unsafe conditions. For your safety, do not enter closed or barricaded areas and follow all posted signs and staff instructions. Crews are working to secure the affected areas and restore safe public access. The closure will remain in effect until conditions are determined to be safe.

title: Closure of Billy Mitchell Airport for Repaving Project
description: The Billy Mitchell Airport (HSE) is closed to accommodate a runway pavement rehabilitation project. The project will provide full resurfacing of paved areas, new reflective paint, and new tie-downs and anchors, improving visitor safety and enhancing the overall visitor experience.

title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
description: As of Thursday, August 13, 2026, the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

title: Reroute in Effect — Skunk and Foster Lakes Segment
description: A reroute is in effect between Indian Valley Rd and Grenlie Rd from September 1, 2026 to January 5, 2027 due to private hunting. Bypass the closure by heading southwest, then south on N Foley Rd, and turning east on Grenlie Rd. The section between Grenlie Rd and Rieben Rd is also closed during the 9‑day gun deer season. title: Reroute in Effect — Thornapple Creek Segment
description: The first 0.4 miles east of Thornapple Creek Rd are closed September 1–December 31 for private hunting. title: Restrooms Closed
description: Castle Clinton restrooms are closed due to a maintenance issue. At the moment, we are not able to determine when they will reopen. Additional public restrooms are available in Battery Park and at the Staten Island Ferry Terminal.

title: Tyler Bend Pavilion Closure
description: Starting on January 20, 2026, the Tyler Bend Pavilion will be closed for construction on the pavilion restrooms. The Tyler Bend Pavilion parking area and Lower Launch River access remain open to the public. The Pavilion is expected to re-open no later than August 31, 2026.

title: A.G Gaston Motel Closed for Construction
description: The 1954 wing of the A.G. Gaston Motel is closed for renovation. Visit the Temporary Visitor Center in the Birmingham Civil Rights Institute at 520 16th St N, Birmingham, AL 35203 open Wednesday–Friday 10 am to 4 pm. The construction is expected to take 18 months. When completed the site will increase accessibility with a new elevator, new exhibits to tell the story of the building and Project C, and revitalize this historic landmark. Follow the link for more information.

title: Tours by appointment unavailable on certain dates in November - January
description: Tours by appointment are not available on the following dates: November: 25-27 December: 24-25, 31 January: 1

title: Fort Spokane boat launch & day use open; Campground open with some closures
description: Fort Spokane Campground has re-opened to the public with minimal closures as of 8/14/2026. Sites 39, 40, 41, 50, and walk-in sites 64-68 will remain closed for the foreseeable future due to fire damage and hazard trees. Caution tape and closure signs have been posted for visitor safety. Please remain in open areas of the campground only. The Fort Spokane day use area and boat launch remain open. Please continue to use caution throughout these areas.

title: Upcoming Site Closure – Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill
description: Starting August 24, the Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill (John Adams and John Quincy Adams Birthplaces) will close for construction on a major cultural landscape project. The entire site will be inaccessible from August 24 through the remainder of the tour season. The Visitor Center and Peace field remain open and accessible.

title: Closures at Little Hunting Creek Bridge Aug. 14 - 17 and Aug. 21 - 24
description: Three of the four lanes on the GWMP at Little Hunting Creek Bridge will close from 6 a.m. Friday, Aug. 14, to 8 a.m. Monday, Aug. 17, and from 6 a.m. Friday, Aug. 21, to 8 a.m. Monday, Aug. 24. Only one lane will remain open during these periods. Flaggers will alternate northbound and southbound traffic through the open lane. Drivers should expect major delays during the Friday morning and evening commutes and the Monday morning commute. Allow extra time or use another route.

title: Temporary Location - Selma Welcome Center Closed
description: Our temporary location for the Selma Interpretive Center is closed until further notice. The Lowndes and Montgomery Interpretive Centers are open Monday through Saturday from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM. For additional information, call us at (334)877-1983 or click "more>" below.

title: Hart Mine Road Closed

title: Hyde Street Pier Closure
description: Hyde Street Pier and access to historic ships will be closed to public until further notice starting 11/04/2024 in preparation for Hyde Street Pier renovation work. Limited public access to the ships is available on Saturdays and Sundays at Mare Island.

title: Selma Interpretive Center Closed
description: The Selma Interpretive Center will remain closed to the public due to major renovations; project completion is expected in 2028. title: Closure: USS Cassin Young

title: Reroute in Effect — Monticello Segment
description: The Stewart Tunnel is closed indefinitely pending reconstruction. The Ice Age Trail is closed at both intersections of Tunnel Rd. Follow Tunnel Rd to bypass the closure and remain on the designated alternate route. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Road damage possible throughout park
description: Use caution when driving through Mojave National Preserve. Widespread storms have potentially flooded or damaged roads throughout the preserve.

title: Select Park Rivers Closed to Fishing
description: The Madison, Firehole and Gibbon (downstream of Norris Campground) rivers are closed to fishing until water temperatures cool to protect the park's native and wild trout fisheries. Most other rivers and streams are open to fishing, as specified in park fishing regulations.

title: Reroute in Effect — Hartman Creek Segment
description: A reroute is in effect between the Emmons Creek Fishery Area and Hartman Creek State Park due to forestry operations. Follow posted signage to remain on the designated reroute. For maps and additional details from the Ice Age Trail Alliance, follow the link below:

title: Bat Tests Positive for Rabies, Visitors Urged to Report Potential Contact
description: A rabid bat was found at Olympic National Park near Staircase Bridge on August 9th. At approximately 2 p.m., the bat swooped down onto an unidentified woman and was temporarily caught in her hair. This individual is at risk for rabies and should seek healthcare immediately, as well as contact the Mason County Health Department at 360-427-9670 ext. 405. More at the link.

title: Experiencing High Temperatures in the Visitor Center
description: While planning your visit to the site please note that we are currently experiencing some high temperatures in the Visitor Center. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause as we work to alleviate the issue.

title: Expect long delays at the Hoh Rainforest
description: Lengthy delays are likely at the Hoh Rainforest entrance station between 7:30 AM - 5 PM. Plan ahead for a 1-3+ hour wait. When the parking lot fills, traffic is metered at the entrance station. Bring what you need for a long wait, and be mindful of not blocking entrances to businesses or homes along the road.

title: Construction Begins on Glenn-Viniard Road in Chickamauga Battlefield
description: Beginning August 12, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park will temporarily close Glenn‑Viniard Road between LaFayette Road and Wilder Road to support construction work in Chickamauga Battlefield. During this period, all public traffic will be prohibited on the closed portion of the road. The park expects the project to be completed by early September 2026. A temporary detour will be implemented to maintain visitor access to the designated battlefield tour routes.

title: Lilly Bluff Overlook Decking Replacement
description: Decking replacement is underway at Lilly Bluff Overlook and is expected to take about six weeks. The overlook will remain open, but some sections will be temporarily closed as repairs are completed.

title: Compost Toilet Removal at KAHO
description: Beginning Monday, August 10, crews will be removing the compost toilet located on the trail between the Petroglyph Boardwalk and ʻAiʻōpio. Work is expected to last approximately two weeks. The trail will remain open during this time. Visitors should use caution when passing through the work area and be aware of equipment, crews, and construction noise. Thank you for your patience and cooperation.

title: Northbound GWMP Lane Closures Begin Aug. 10 Between Spout Run and Route 123
description: Northbound lanes between Spout Run Parkway and Route 123 will close Mondays through Thursdays  from 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.  from Aug. 10 – Sept. 1 for tree maintenance.

title: Primary Phone Line is Experiencing Intermittent Service Disruptions
description: The primary phone line is experiencing intermittent service disruptions. If you are unable to reach staff, please email us at libi_information@nps.gov. Please understand that emails will not be answered immediately. The park's website will have the most up-to-date information.

title: All Backpacks Must be in Storage Area at Three Mile and Rock Harbor.
description: All backpacks must be stored in backpack storage areas at Three Mile and Rock Harbor campgrounds. All food and scented items are to be in the Food Storage Lockers. Containers should be kept in the Food Storage Locker when space allows or near the Food Storage Locker, do not store in tents.

title: Accessibility Lifts Out of Service at Fort Sumter
description: The mobility lifts at Fort Sumter on the second and third levels are currently out of order. The bottom level of the fort, along with the water fountain, remains wheelchair accessible.

title: History House at Sandy Hook Closed to the Public
description: The History House at Sandy Hook will be closed for maintenance from Monday August 17 through Friday August 21, 2026.

title: Heat Alert - Temperatures May Be Higher Than Forecast
description: Actual temperatures in the park may be up to 6℉ (3 ℃) higher than forecasts provided by the National Weather Service (NWS). Temperatures in rocky, exposed areas may be up to 10℉ (6 ℃) hotter than the actual temperature. Please plan accordingly, stay hydrated, limit strenuous activity during the hottest parts of the day, and be prepared for extreme heat conditions.

title: Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: To ensure public safety and to provide the highest degree of protection to park resources, fire restrictions are in effect until further notice.

title: Air Quality Impacted by Wildfire Smoke
description: Smoke from regional wildfires is affecting air quality in the park. When air quality is a concern be sure to: 1) monitor air quality and smoke forecasts 2) assess your own sensitivity to poor air quality, and the sensitivity of others in your group and 3) adjust outdoor activities as needed. Find out current air quality conditions at https://fire.airnow.gov.

title: Rend Trail Closed through December 2027
description: The Rend Trail is closed for trail Improvements that will include a new parking area, restroom, and a small picnic area overlooking Arbuckle Creek at the Minden trailhead, structural improvements to five historic railroad trestles along the trail, and full trail surface rehabilitation. Additionally, construction of a large accessible ramp over the ‘big rock’ will replace a stairway, resulting in the only fully accessible earthen surface trail located within the park.

title: Fire Ban in Effect
description: Effective Thursday, August 6 building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire, or campfire, charcoal grill, tiki torches, incense burners, candles, propane campfire, wood burning stoves, and devices using pressurized liquid or gas is prohibited. This includes the designated fire rings at South Beach. Propane fire pits are not allowed during the ban.

title: Full Burn Ban Begins August 7
description: Due to increased fire activity and dry vegetation, all campfires will be prohibited starting on August 7. This includes wilderness, backcountry, non-developed and developed areas, and coastal beaches. Propane and gas stoves are allowed, if operated at least three feet away from flammable vegetation and forest litter.

title: Ocean Beach Fire Season in Effect through October 31, 2026
description: Fires allowed ONLY in park provided concrete fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20. Do NOT make fire rings using rocks, logs or other items. When the Bay Area Air Quality Management District declares a Spare the Air Day, NO campfires, beach fires, or outdoor grills are allowed in the park. For more information, visit the beach fire regulations link below.

title: El Calderon Trail closed for construction through September 2026
description: The El Calderon Trail and parking area are closed from August 2025 through September 2026 for a major improvement project. NPS Road 100 will remain open for local traffic only, and the Continental Divide Trail will remain open for CDT thru-hikers.

title: Smoke from Wildfires May Affect Air Quality
description: Smoke from wildfires is to be expected with active fires across the region.Take precautions when recreating outdoors when heavy smoke is present.

title: Project Safety Closure in Place Near Southernmost Groin in Buxton
description: Public access is closed for 300 feet north and south of a groin repair project site in Buxton, as well as the adjacent ocean area to the east. Surfers, swimmers, and all other recreationists should stay at least 300 feet from the southernmost groin area for safety purposes.

title: 44 Creek Bridge Failure
description: 44 creek bridge is closed due to damage identified by a Federal Highway inspection team. This bridge is north of 44 Camp, approximately 7 miles south of the Redwood Creek trailhead and about 1 mile north of the Tall Trees river crossing. All trails remain open in the area, but crossing this ravine is dangerous and not advised. Hikers should plan to take alternative routes to 44 Camp, which will add at least 3.5 miles from Redwood Creek Trailhead. Stop by a visitor center for more information.

title: Temporary Closure of the Llyod W. Smith Gallery in the Museum
description: The Llyod W. Smith Gallery will be closed temporarily due to construction. All other exhibits will remain open.

title: McQueen's Island Trail Closed Beginning August 3, 2026
description: The McQueen's Island Trail will close for a Chatham County restoration project beginning August 3, 2026.

title: Fleener Chimney Area Closed
description: Due to increased wasp activity the Fleener Chimney is closed effective August 3, 2026, until further notice.

title: Air quality impacted by wildfire smoke.
description: Smoke from regional wildfires is affecting air quality in the park. When air quality is a concern: 1. monitor air quality and smoke forecasts; 2. assess your own sensitivity to poor air quality, and the sensitivity of others in your group; 3. adjust outdoor activities as needed.

title: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center Phone Out of Order
description: The Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center phone line (718-318-4340) is not working at this time. Please monitor social media (Instagram and Facebook) or contact our general park information line at 718-354-4606 or Gateway_feedback@nps.gov for program or other park updates. For emergencies, call U.S. Park Police dispatch at 718-354-4700.

title: Current Park Closures
description: Closures may occur due to inclement weather, construction projects, or other emergency conditions. Please visit the linked page for information about current closures.

title: Temporary Closure of Park Areas at the Request of US Secret Service
description: At the request of the United States Secret Service and to ensure necessary security and safety for the adjacent White House complex and its occupants, several designated areas of President's Park will be temporarily closed from approximately 12:00 a.m. on Saturday, August 1, 2026, until approximately 11:59 p.m. on Monday, August 31, 2026. For a closure map and more detailed information, please follow the link below.

title: Smokey air from local wildfires
description: Current air quality is being influenced by local fires and can change in an instant. Check https://www.airnow.gov/ for specific air quality index (AQI) information for your favorite spot at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area.

title: Lindenwald Opens for 2026 Season
description: Lindenwald Tours – 2026 Season Lindenwald is open for tours Friday–Sunday at 10 AM, 11 AM, 1 PM, and 3 PM. Tours are first-come, first-served. Monday–Thursday: grounds are open, but no tours are available. Park stamps, and restrooms are available in the Visitor Center.

title: Accessible Lift Inoperable at Parsonage
description: The accessible wheelchair lift for the Parsonage building is undergoing maintenance as of 7/10/26. Visitors who are unable to use stairs may not be able to enter the parsonage until this issue is resolved.

title: Stage 1 Fire Restrictions
description: Stage 1 fire restrictions in effect as of July 31, 2026. Use of portable gas stoves is permitted. Prohibited Actions: No open fires, No smoking outdoors within 3 feet of vegetation, No welding or similar devices, No flares, fireworks, etc.

title: Scam Warning: Book Ferry Tickets Through Authorized Concessioner Only
description: The National Park Service is aware of fraudulent websites selling invalid ferry tickets to Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park. Valid ferry tickets can only be purchased through the park's authorized concessioner at www.fortsumtertours.com. Visitors should carefully verify the website address before purchasing tickets. Tickets purchased through unauthorized websites are not valid and will not be honored.

title: Construction on North Park Road
description: Construction underway on North Park Road between Leeks Marina and Lizard Creek Campground. 15-min delays both directions 6am-9pm / 1-hour delays both directions 9pm-6am. The section of road is about 7 miles north of Colter Bay and 11.5 miles south of Yellowstone.

title: Parts of Santa Rosa Island Closed During Wildfire Recovery
description: Santa Rosa Island reopens to limited day use on July 1. No overnight visits are allowed. Burned areas, including Water Canyon Campground, remain closed through at least September 15. Click the more link for additional information.

title: Partial Beach Closures in Place in Front of Buxton Village
description: The beachfront in front of Buxton Village is temporarily closed due to the presence of threatened oceanfront structures and Dare County's beach nourishment project. Renourished sections of beach will open to the public immediately after construction activities conclude in the areas, generally within 24 hours.

title: Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: All campfires and open flames are prohibited throughout the monument, including in Indian Well campground. Devices that burn wood, charcoal, pellets or biomass are not allowed. Gas or pressurized stoves (propane, butane or similar are permitted if they have a shut-off valve.

title: Juniper Lake Campground Closed
description: The Juniper Lake Campground and day use area is currently closed for maintenance and campground improvement projects. Potable water is not available in the campground. The Juniper Lake Road (access to lake and trailheads) is open. Please drive with caution as road crews and contractors may be actively working along the roadway.

title: Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Due to high fire danger, fire restrictions are in effect in all areas of Lassen Volcanic National Park. Building, maintaining, attending, or using open fires, campfires, or stove fires is prohibited, including charcoal. Self-contained propane or petroleum camp stoves are permitted.

title: Schonchin Butte Closure
description: Schonchin Butte Road and Trail are closed to all traffic when the gate is closed, due to maintenance work occurring at the fire lookout.

title: Alternate Route for Access to Root Glacier
description: The old route to access Root Glacier is no longer safe due to unstable ground. An alternative, new route exists past the Amazon Creek. Seek information at the visitor center or news release webpage.

title: Fire Restrictions
description: Due to the continued fire danger in Southern Oregon, Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve has instituted a full fire ban. To ensure public safety and to provide the highest degree of protection to park resources, the Fire Ban prohibits Campfires. Wood and charcoal fires are NOT allowed in Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve.

title: Lifeguards at Herring Cove Beach Weekends ONLY
description: Lifeguards will be present at Herring Cove Beach on weekends ONLY until August 23. Pay attention to signage and swim at your own risk on weekdays.

title: Fire Ban
description: City of Rocks is under fire restrictions effective 07/30/26 until further notice. Campers MAY NOT have a wood campfire. Campers MAY NOT use a self-providing gas-fueled fire ring. Campers MAY NOT use charcoal. Campers may use gas-fueled grills/stoves for cooking.

title: Dingmans Falls Trail, Road, and Access Closed for Bridge Replacement
description: Dingmans Falls site is closed for a bridge replacement project and trail rehabilitation. All traffic, including pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle traffic, is prohibited on the road and trail during construction.

title: Construction Activity at Meyers Beach; Visitor and Kayak Access Maintained
description: Construction has begun on the Meyers Beach Access Path Project. Access to the beach and parking lot will remain open, but visitors should expect construction noise and closed lawn areas for staging. Kayak groups should move gear directly to the beach to reduce congestion. The project will upgrade the existing staircase to include a universally designed path, improving access to the beach and kayak launch for all visitors.

title: Stage 2 Burn Restrictions
description: All campfires are prohibited. Devices using pressurized liquid or gas (stoves, grills or lanterns) that include shut-off valves are permitted when used in an area at least three feet or more from flammable material such as grasses or pine needles. Smoking is only allowed in an enclosed vehicle.

title: Grand View Point Closed for Construction Weekdays July 27 to Oct 1
description: Grand View Point Overlook, Grand View Point Trail, and 0.3 mi (0.5 km) of park road is closed Monday to Thursday. The closure applies to all uses, including vehicles, tour buses, motorcycles, bikes, & hikers. Parking is open but limited Friday to Sunday.

title: Bridge to Maryland Heights & C&O Canal CLOSED
description: The NPS is rehabilitating the stairway connecting the Goodloe Byron Memorial Footbridge to the C&O Canal NHP towpath. The stairway will be CLOSED beginning July 27 for approximately one month while crews install the new stairwell. A shuttle will run between C&O Canal Lock 34 and Harpers Ferry National Historical Park Visitor Center. This will impact access to Maryland Heights, the Appalachian NST, and the Potomac Heritage NST.

title: Jockey Hollow Outer Blue Loop and a Section of Primrose Trail Closed
description: Following storms on 7/3/2026, many park trails were closed due to blowdown of trees and hazardous conditions. As of 7/27/2026 most trails are passable. The Mount Kimble Trail (Outer Blue Loop) remains closed as well as a section of the Primrose Trail (Red Trail). Please check in at the Visitor Center for more information and take caution as summer storms continue to cause tree falls. Report any fallen trees to a Park Ranger.

title: Passaic River Bridge Trail (Teal Trail) Closed
description: The Passaic River Bridge Trail is closed between Tempe Wick Road and the Cross Estate in the New Jersey Brigade area due to construction of a new bridge.

title: Monsoon Season & Flash Floods
description: Heavy rains can cause sudden flooding, especially in canyons and washes. Do not drive or hike through flood waters. Get to high ground and wait for floods to subside. Some roads may close temporarily; closures are posted at the visitor center.

title: Trail update 7/25/26
description: Most trails are open and ready for the public. Those that remain closed are the Charleston Road/ Goudey Trail past the Cherokee Path and the portion of Cherokee Path between the stockade fort and the Charleston Road.

title: Bicycles and Pedestrians now allowed on Volcano Road
description: Capulin Volcano Highway is now a roadway shared by multiple users that include vehicles, hikers, bikers, walkers and runners. Dogs on a minimum 6-foot leash are also allowed on the roadway. Be watchful of others that are present on the highway. Follow the new traffic flow signs and keep vehicle and bicycle speeds at the posted speed limits of 20 mph in general and 10 mph in the S curves. Let’s all stay safe!

title: Trail Closure
description: A portion of the Headland Trail is closed due to ongoing restoration work. Access to the trail will now close at 2:30 pm daily. All hikers must be off the trails by 4:45 pm.

title: Temporary Emergency Fire Closure
description: Open fires of any kind, including charcoal fires, are prohibited until conditions improve. Smoking is prohibited except for in vehicles or buildings where indicated. Use of gas stoves is permitted in areas that are clear of flammable materials.

title: Visitor Center Open at 419 Decatur Street
description: The New Orleans Jazz NHP & Jean Lafitte NHP&P have a combined French Quarter Visitor Center at 419 Decatur Street. Open Tuesdays through Saturdays, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. Calendar for events: https://www.nps.gov/jazz/planyourvisit/calendar.

title: Partial Trail Closure
description: The crossover trail through the center of the historic area, near the flagpole, is temporarily closed for safety. The remainder of the main park trail is open.

title: Harmful Algae Bloom
description: A Harmful Algae Bloom has been confirmed in recent water samples taken from the Nelson's Landing and the Cottonwood Cove areas on Lake Mohave. To reduce health risks, the National Park Service recommends recreators limit body contact with these waters when algae is present. Please click here for pictures of this dangerous cyanobacteria and contact the Park at 702-293-8990 for updates on this advisory.

title: Outer Island Nighttime Closure
description: Outer Island is closed to all use from 10 PM to 6 AM due to bear activity and food‑storage concerns. Day use is permitted outside these hours. The closure remains in effect until further notice to protect visitor safety and support ongoing wildlife management.

title: Trail Closure - Dunewood Trace
description: Temporary closure of the Dunewood Trace trail (2.2 miles), between Kemil Rd, and the Dunewood Campground (near the recycle bins), is now in effect until further notice due to construction of the new Marquette Greenway trail.

title: Upper Fort Mason Roads and Parking Area Closures Fall 2025 - Fall 2026
description: Roads and parking areas at upper Fort Mason will have closures during utilities and seismic retrofit projects. Closures planned Fall 2025 through Fall 2026. Lots will be fenced and used as staging areas for projects occurring at Fort Mason. Signs will be posted in advance of utilities work as project progresses through each area at Fort Mason. Read signs and do not park in posted areas. Vehicles will be towed at owner's expense.

title: 8/3/26 - 8/28/26 Closure at Devils Kitchen Picnic Area Parking Lot
description: From 8/3/26 to 8/28/26, contractors will be repairing and replacing the waterline at Devils Kitchen Picnic Area and parking lot. The restrooms, water, and parking area will be closed throughout the duration of the project. Access to Serpents Trail will remain open at the Devils Kitchen Trailhead.

title: No Lifeguards at Race Point Beach
description: There are no lifeguards on duty at Race Point Beach. Swim at your own risk.

title: Construction for Seawall Project
description: Starting July 27, 2026, Castillo de San Marcos National Monument will begin construction to replace, raise and rehabilitate the park’s failing seawalls. The historic fort will remain accessible throughout the project. Some areas outside of the fort will be closed for safety.

title: LBJ Ranch Reopened Sunday, July 19.
description: Following the flooding which took place July 16, the LBJ Ranch reopened for normal operational hours (9am to 5pm) on Sunday, July 19. The ranch driving route is fully open, and visitors will be able to enter the Junction School and Showbarn as well as view the cemetery and walk to the Reconstructed Birthplace. The sites in the Johnson City District of the park remain open; this includes the national park visitor center and Boyhood Home.

title: Stockton Island Trail Access
description: The trail between Presque Isle Bay and Quarry Bay on Stockton Island is open, but a footbridge on the western portion of the trail was washed out in a 2024 storm. Visitors must wade through shallow water or take an alternate route.

title: Ongoing Closure Notices
description: Devils Island dock and campsites and West Bay Club on Sand Island are closed. These closures affect only a small portion of the Lakeshore. Enjoy your visit.

title: Home of FDR - Partial Closure of Rose Garden
description: The planting beds, lawns, and paths of the Rose Garden will be under construction from late March 2026 lasting through fall of 2026. This rehabilitation will restore the crisp, level character of the garden, improve access and infrastructure, and re-install historic rose and peony varieties. During this period, the Burial Site viewing area should remain available, but occasional disruptions may restrict public access. The graves, marble monument, pet graves, and sundial will not be impacted by this project.

title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes Montezuma Well and the trail to see Montezuma Castle. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes the Pueblo Trail and Tavasci Marsh Trail. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

title: Visitor Center Contact Phone Down
description: The Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace contact phone, (212) 260-1616, is currently experiencing issues. Rangers may not be able to receive your call. For questions, please email thrb_info@nps.gov.

title: East Portal Road
description: Until further notice, East Portal Road and campground are closed due to flood damage.

title: East Portal Road
description: Until further notice, East Portal Road and campground are closed due to flood damage.

title: Poor Air Quality
description: Due to wildfires in the region around the park visitors should expect varying levels of poor air quality due to smoke. For current air quality check the fire and smoke map here: https://fire.airnow.gov/

title: No Water Available at Ok-A-Beh Marina - Flushing Restrooms Closed
description: Due to a water shortage, flushable toilets are currently unavailable at the Ok-A-Beh Marina. Vault toilets are available at the upper parking lot and a floating restroom is available on the courtesy dock.

title: Construction at Blow-Me-Down Mill
description: The area around the Blow-Me-Down Mill and Dam are temporarily closed through August due to work to repair and reinforce the foundation of the Blow-Me-Down Mill.

title: Construction Activity at Little Sand Bay; Boat and Kayak Access Maintained
description: Construction for the Little Sand Bay Marina Rehabilitation Project begins May 1. The Town of Russell boat launch and the NPS kayak beach will remain open, with short detours around work areas. Expect reduced parking, delays, and increased noise. The Little Sand Bay Visitor Center will be closed in 2026 due to construction.

title: Sculptor's Studio Heat Advisory
description: The Sculptor’s Studio may close temporarily during periods of high heat to protect visitors and staff. Please check with park staff upon arrival for the most up‑to‑date information on whether the Studio is open or closed.

title: Avoid Water Contact at Sand Beach Lagoon (Not for Sand Beach)
description: Bacterial levels have exceeded public health standards at Sand Beach Lagoon and a Public Health Advisory has been posted. The public is advised against swimming at this beach until bacterial levels return to healthful levels. (Not for Sand Beach.)

title: Bighorn Lake Elevation is Below 3625ft
description: When lake levels are below 3625, boaters are advised to avoid areas south of Horseshoe Bend and the South Narrows due to low water levels. Throughout the year, lake water levels fluctuate greatly. Hazards and launching abilities change with the water levels. Please use caution when recreating on Bighorn Lake.

title: Sections of moat wall closed until Winter 2026
description: Sections of the moat wall that were damaged by Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024) are undergoing repair and reinforcement. For your safety, please follow posted signage and do not cross any barricades.

title: Fire Danger VERY HIGH
description: Wood-burning fires and charcoal grills are prohibited. Propane and gas stoves allowed only in campground and picnic areas for cooking food. No smoking on trail. No roadside parking. Fireworks are always prohibited.

title: Current Alerts and Conditions
description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

title: Solstice Canyon Trail Weekday Closure for Repairs
description: Solstice Canyon Trail will be closed Monday through Thursday starting July 13, 2026, while crews complete repair work. During closure hours, visitors must enter and exit via Rising Sun Trail. All trails remain open on weekends (including Fridays). The project is expected to last approximately four weeks.

title: Accessible Parking Available
description: Accessible parking is available at the George Washington Carver Museum and The Oaks. For George Washington Carver Museum, after receiving your visitor pass, enter Tuskegee University through Lincoln Gates on Booker T. Washington Boulevard. Pass Margaret Murray Washington Hall and the Kellogg Hotel and Conference Center, then turn right to the parking garage. Accessible parking for The Oaks is at 1200 West Montgomery Road. For assistance, call Sheryl Buchanan at (334) 421-3246

title: Phones Down at the Tuskegee Airmen National Historic Site
description: For any general inquiries and reservations, visitors can contact Ranger Tommy Smith at (334) 421-0340.

title: Status of Cascading Fountain at Meridian Hill Park
description: We appreciate your patience as we work to remove the sediment from the Meridian Hill Cascading Fountain. The discoloration occurred when two long-unused water lines were brought back online as part of our continuing effort to fine-tune the fountain’s operations. Visitors should begin seeing the fountain’s signature sparkling water again soon.

title: No cold-water flow at the Serpentine Hot Springs bathhouse
description: There is currently no cold-water flow into the tub at Serpentine Hot Springs. Please proceed with caution. The National Park Service plans to complete repairs on the cold‑water pipe in August. Visitors are respectfully advised not to dig ditches or otherwise attempt to establish alternative cold‑water access. Thank you for your cooperation.

title: Detour along Mount Vernon Trail at Gravelly Point
description: Due to constriction for the Long Bridge Project, the Mount Vernon Trail will be temporarily detoured around the construction zone beginning on July 15, 2026. Trail users should expect periodic crossings of equipment and materials where the trail meets the construction access road. Detour will be in place through 2030.

title: Areas of Meridian Hill Park closed for turf restoration
description: The turf at Meridian Hill Park is closed through August 17 while we make the park safer and more enjoyable for everyone. Thank you for your patience.

title: Wind Cave Canyon Trail Closed for Repair and Improvement
description: Wind Cave Canyon Trail is closed so that the trail and adjoining road can be repaired from frequent washouts. Sixteen low water crossings will be hardened and the road resurfaced. The trail could be closed for several weeks. This closure does not affect any cave tours.

title: Fire Operations
description: Wildfires are occurring in the region. Water scooping airplanes are using the reservoir. Please use caution and stay clear of areas where water scooping operations are occurring.

title: Do not pick up hitchhikers
description: Do not pick up hitchhikers. Please report their locations to law enforcement by calling 911.

title: Church & under trees in high wind conditions
description: Avoid area around the church & under trees in high wind conditions

title: Sidewalk scaffolding at Federal Hall
description: Protective sidewalk scaffolding has been erected around the building as a safety precaution.

title: Phone lines working intermittently
description: Our phone lines are working intermittently. If you are not able to reach us by phone, please email us at bela_information@nps.gov.

title: Roadway Work to Begin at Sanford Yake Campgournd Monday, July 13th
description: The National Park Service announces that Federal Highway Administration contractors will begin roadway and pavement maintenance at Sanford Yake Campground starting Monday, July 13, 2026. This project will include chip seal, micro seal, micro surfacing, and pavement striping throughout key areas of Lake Meredith National Recreation Area. Visitors to Alibates Flint Quarries National Monument and Lake Meredith National Recreation Area are encouraged to follow all posted message boards and traffic instructions.

title: Roadwork to Begin at Sanford Yake Campground Monday, July 13th
description: The National Park Service announces that Federal Highway Administration contractors will begin roadway and pavement maintenance at Sanford Yake Campground starting Monday, July 13, 2026. This project will include chip seal, micro seal, micro surfacing, and pavement striping throughout key areas of Lake Meredith National Recreation Area. Visitors to Alibates Flint Quarries National Monument and Lake Meredith National Recreation Area are encouraged to follow all posted message boards and traffic instructions.

title: Paving Work Ongoing Throughout the Park
description: Paving work is being done throughout Ozark National Scenic Riverways during the 2026 summer season, including at Alley Spring, Round Spring, Pulltite, and Big Spring. Watch here and on our park Facebook page for updates, as roads and campground loops may close and reopen depending on work progress.

title: Round Spring Pavilion Parking Area Closed
description: The parking lot for the Round Spring Pavilion and for Round Spring itself is CLOSED for the remainder of the 2026 summer season while the low water bridge over Spring Valley Creek is rebuilt. Alternative parking near Round Spring Group Campsites 4-8 will provide trail access to the north side of Round Spring.

title: Round Spring Lower River Landing Closed
description: The lower river landing at Round Spring, located in the campground, is closed until further notice for paving. Floaters putting in or taking out at Round Spring should plan to use the upper landing behind Carr's Store.

title: Total Fire Restrictions Implemented June 20, 2026
description: Due to extreme fire conditions, all fires at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area are prohibited effective 12:01 a.m., June 20, until further notice. No open flames are permitted. Only self-contained propane or gas cookstoves and lanterns are allowed during the full fire ban.

title: Stehekin is Open, Services Limited at Stehekin Landing
description: Visitor and recreational opportunities continue to be available in the Stehekin Valley. Some services are limited at the Stehekin Landing following flood damage in December 2025.

title: Mora Road Closed for Essential Repairs
description: Mora Road is closed to all traffic, including bicycles and pedestrians, at the campground. Rialto Beach is not accessible via Mora Road during this construction period. Mora Campground is open. This construction work will repair damage from a severe winter flood event, fortify the road against river migration, and protect long-term access to Rialto Beach.

title: Fort Jay front gate only — Temporary Closure.
description: The FRONT GATE of Fort Jay is temporarily closed to all. The fort is currently open to visitation Wednesday thru Sunday 10am to 4pm. Access to the fort will be via the western or rear sallyport.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Fire danger is extremely high. No fires (charcoal or wood) are permitted anywhere in the park, including in the campground. No smoking outside of your vehicle. Fireworks are always banned. Check vehicles for dragging chains. Be safe and fire aware!

title: Staircase Developed Area is Open, Use Caution in Burned Areas
description: The Staircase developed area is open. The surrounding wilderness areas will remain closed as repair and recovery efforts continue. Use extreme caution when entering burned areas. Burned landscapes may contain falling trees and branches, loose boulders, unstable ground, stump holes, landslides, and debris flows. Changing conditions such as wind, rain, or storms can rapidly trigger hazards. Learn more on our Fire Conditions and Updates page.

title: Kennesaw Mountain Dr. Closed to Private Vehicles and Cyclists
description: Starting January 5th, 2026, the road to the top of Kennesaw Mountain will be closed to private vehicles and cyclists due to construction and painting. Shuttle service to the top of the mountain is ONLY available on weekends and select federal holidays. The park's Visitor Center is still accessible. This work is in preparation for the upcoming Safety Improvement Project. For updates, continue to check park's website.

title: Partial Closures to Little Calumet River Trail and Glenwood Dunes Trail
description: Marquette Greenway construction will require closing sections of the Glenwood Dunes Trail (April–December 2026) and Little Calumet River / Mnoké Prairie Trail (May–December 2026). Closure dates may shift as work progresses. Please follow all posted closures and check the park website or NPS App for updates.

title: Hobart Woodland Trail Temporary Closure
description: Hobart Woodland is closed until further notice while park crews work to clear several downed trees that are creating hazardous conditions for visitors.

title: Munising Falls Trail Closed Until Further Notice
description: The Munising Falls Trail within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore is closed until further notice. Approximately 75-feet of the paved trail was washed out April 28th from recent heavy rainfall and seasonal snow melt.

title: Church Loop Trail Closure
description: The Church Loop Trail in the Thurmond area of the park is temporarily closed due to downed trees.

title: Stage 2 fire restrictions in effect
description: No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires and charcoal fires in Watchman Campground, South Campground, and picnic areas in Zion Canyon. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions in effect - campfires banned
description: Stage II Fire Restrictions are in effect at Great Basin National Park. Due to extreme fire danger, campfires, charcoal grills, and outdoor smoking are prohibited throughout the park. Gas and liquid-fueled stoves are permitted.

title: Yosemite Traffic Updates
description: When the park is very busy, you can get updates on current traffic conditions in Yosemite by texting ynptraffic to 333111.

title: Guided Tours Available by Appointment Only
description: To request a guided tour, please contact the park a minimum of two weeks in advance. The grounds and outbuildings of Oakland Plantation and Magnolia Plantation are open for self-guided tours from 9:00 am to 3:30 pm Wednesday through Sunday.

title: Food Storage Regulations in Effect
description: Proper food storage is required on Isle Royale. All food, trash, scented items, cooking supplies, cooking utensils, and fish/fish parts must be stored properly. To learn more about food storage and to learn how to properly store your food, trash, and scented items, click "more."

title: Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion
description: The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024.

title: Arlington House Potential Closures
description: Due to HVAC system issues, Arlington House may close to visitors when interior temperatures reach 85°F. Temporary closures may occur with little notice to protect the safety and comfort of visitors and staff.

title: East Rim Drive is CLOSED from Park Headquarters to Phantom Ship Overlook
description: East Rim Drive is currently CLOSED to all public access from Park Headquarters to Phantom Ship Overlook for road construction. West Rim Drive, North Entrance Road, East Rim Drive from North Junction to Phantom Ship Overlook, Cloudcap Road, and Pinnacles Road are now OPEN for travel.

title: Mainland Museum Closure
description: The Cumberland Island Museum will be closed for an extended period due to roof leakages. We apologize for any inconvenience but look forward to reopening to you in the future.

title: Stage II Fire Restrictions
description: Stage II fire restrictions are in effect until further notice. Campfires including charcoal are not permitted, even in established fire rings. Smoking is only permitted within an enclosed vehicle. Gas or liquid fueled portable camp stoves are still permitted.

title: Cave Tour Reservations
description: Advance cave tour reservations up until August 31st are available. September reservations will become available on August 1st. Reservations are strongly recommended. Reservations full? Choose a day to come to the park early in the day to purchase a same day cave tour ticket.

title: Partial Trail Closure at Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk
description: Closed portion of Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk Trail along Burns Waterway due to unsafe conditions from erosional damage. This trail portion will remain closed while funding is sought for repair work. Pier access remains open on either side of closure.

title: Wood & Charcoal Burn Ban
description: To protect park infrastructure and visitors during this hot, dry period of year, wood and charcoal/briquette burning is temporarily banned. Propane grills are still okay. Thank you for recreating responsibly in your national recreation area.

title: Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Until further notice, the following are PROHIBITED in all park areas: (1) Building, maintaining, attending, or using a fire or campfire, including charcoal fires or pellet grills, or any other open burning. Properly shielded, self-contained propane or liquid-fueled camp stoves and grills, lanterns, or other heated devices with on/off switches are permitted. (2) All smoking, except within a personally-owned enclosed vehicle. (3) Discharging or using any kind of fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices.

title: A Fire Ban (Stage 2 Fire Restrictions) Are In Effect
description: Due to very high fire danger, the extended weather forecast, and current fire activity in the State of Colorado, Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are now in effect within Rocky Mountain National Park. When Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are in effect, this means that all campfires, including charcoal briquette fires are not permitted anywhere within Rocky Mountain National Park. This ban is effective beginning today, June 29, and will remain in effect until further notice.

title: Be cautious around park rivers & learn how to cross safely!
description: Many hikers underestimate the power of moving water. Regardless of your knowledge, skills, and experience use these pointers in making wise decisions before attempting to cross a river.

title: Elevated E. Coli levels - Fremont River
description: Recent water quality testing shows elevated E. coli levels in the Fremont River. Use caution if entering the water. Do not get water in your mouth, do not swim. Wash hands with soap and water.

title: Current Alerts and Conditions
description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: All fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles or in developed areas over 3 feet from flammables.

title: Phone Number not Working
description: The phone at the park (435-692-1234) is not functioning reliably. People are advised to call 435-241-3951 during business hours in order to speak with a ranger.

title: Park Headquarters Road is closed
description: Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.

title: Notice of Stage II Fire Restriction Order in Effect
description: No building, maintaining, attending or using a fire or campfire in all areas of the monument, including charcoal fires. Properly shielded gas or liquid-fueled portable camp stoves are allowed. Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle. Discharging or using fireworks or other pyrotechnic devices are always prohibited on all federal public land.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: Due to the extremely dry conditions and high fire danger all fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry/river campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles.

title: Annual/Seasonal Canyoneering Closures
description: The following are closed to entry through 8/31/2026 to protect sensitive resources: the heads of Fivemile Wash & Burro Wash descending east 2 miles; Shinob Canyon + all routes descending into Shinob (including Na-gah, Nighthawk, & Timpie); and Arch Nemesis Canyon, including the route exiting at Capitol Gorge + all direct tributary canyons.

title: Two Medicine North Shore Trailhead Reroute
description: In 2026, Two Medicine's North Shore Trailhead is not accessible due to construction in the Two Medicine Campground. A reroute has been established to access the North Shore Trail but does require a ford (unbridged water crossing). Directional signage is in place marking the reroute. Hikers may also access Twin Falls, Upper Two Medicine Lake, No Name Lake, and Dawson Pass without a ford, by using the South Shore Trail. Note: this adds approximately 1 mile of distance, one-way.

title: No Wood or Charcoal Fires Allowed - Stage 2 Fire Restrictions in Effect
description: All fires are prohibited. Only petroleum or propane-fueled stoves or grills are allowed in backcountry campsites, campgrounds, and picnic areas. Fireworks are never allowed. Smoke only inside vehicles or in developed areas over 3 feet from flammables.

title: Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures
description: Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability.

title: What's Closed and What's Open: South Rim & North Rim
description: Visit this link for a list of the available visitor services in Grand Canyon Village, Desert View, and the North Rim.

title: Parkwide Fire Ban in effect until further notice beginning June 26
description: Beginning Friday 6/26/26 until rescinded, a parkwide fire ban is implemented for all campfires & the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, & BBQ grills.

title: Big South Fork’s Brewster Bridge Road to Temporarily Close for Repair
description: Brewster Bridge Road in Big South Fork NRRA will temporarily close for repair and re-pavement beginning on Monday, June 29. The road was heavily damaged from significant rain events in 2022 and 2023. The area boat launch and day use area will be inaccessible during the project.

title: Campfire Ban in All Portions of the Park Complex Begins June 29
description: Effective Monday, June 29, campfires or the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, and barbeque grills, are banned in all portions of North Cascades National Park Service Complex, which includes North Cascades National Park, Ross Lake National Recreation Area, and Lake Chelan National Recreation Area.. This applies to anything that produces ash, including charcoal grills. Propane fire pits are not allowed during the ban.

title: Patriots Point Ferries Accessibility Information
description: Ferries to Fort Sumter from Patriots Point are not always accessible for individuals who use mobility assistance devices or have trouble navigating stairs. The Fort Sumter Visitor Center departure location is fully accessible or visitors can call Fort Sumter Tours (843-722-2628) for current Patriots Point accessibility conditions.

title: Going-to-the-Sun Road is Open for 2026 Season
description: The Going-to-the-Sun Road is fully open for the 2026 summer season. The road may now be accessed by motorized vehicles over Logan Pass from both the West Glacier and St. Mary Entrances.

title: Areas of Meridian Hill Park closed for repairs
description: Much of the upper level of the park is closed to rehabilitate the grass. Fountains and the reflecting pool are open but may be turned off or drained occasionally for maintenance. The reflecting pool will undergo repairs June 20-28. Visit the Meridian Hill Park page for more information.

title: Please use caution when visiting park grounds.
